observations.note: Corrected for the same reason and in the same milestone as depth_format.ruby_enum_mapping: Graphics::RasterizerState now exists, so the fourth element of that census is true. It holds no vertex buffer, no index buffer and no effect, and draws nothing, so what this row asserts is unchanged -- the other four are still false and no primitive, topology or draw_ symbol is bound. Pre-correction SHA-256 of this file 0d020e76733b512d21b7f842a870369d966ec0e9d5aa6fe49b93581b5ad80b41, of the replayed aggregate fd6105726e06101ef043a23dfefc0c597d35264d4fb689fb0db42c29a53cb7d5. Corrected again when VertexDeclaration was built: the third element of the same census is now true too. It holds no vertex buffer and draws nothing -- its own IL reaches the renderer only through the assembly-visible Bind/Unbind the contract never selects -- so what this row asserts is unchanged, and the two elements left false are VertexBuffer and IndexBuffer, which are what a draw call would really need. Pre-correction SHA-256 of this file e4395db1e47f12336b2a948a974ddaedda2d460a811927d33ee2eacfe56aa160, of the replayed aggregate b977ca28ffe94df5976ace4d6a8b1109ffec46ed360f6b512f83ba66c7cc8836. Corrected a third time when SpriteBatch.DrawString was built: the last element -- 'is any route named primitive or draw_ bound?' -- is now true, because cna_sprite_batch_draw_string is. It draws text through a SpriteBatch interval rather than a primitive topology, so what this row asserts about PrimitiveType is unchanged: no primitive or topology constant exists, no draw method is defined on GraphicsDevice, and no vertex or index buffer is projected. The fragment was always too broad for the claim it was carrying, and the test beside this row now checks draw_primitive and draw_user instead. Pre-correction SHA-256 of the aggregate 4809f249967026ada710963e70b425ca87ea46fac33920c1065d6e05af549ae6, of the per-milestone file db3fbfa920bff31b87eda34683d68655a64751e95e957c33ec0ad6d937b008cc. Corrected a fifth time when the vertex and index buffers were built: the first two elements of that census are now true as well, so every one of the five is. The census has stopped discriminating and this correction retires it as evidence rather than repairing it -- what the row asserts about `PrimitiveType` is carried by the elements around it, which are unchanged: no primitive or topology constant is bound, `GraphicsDevice` defines none of the five Draw* members, and the enum still takes its values from its own IL. A buffer holds vertices; drawing them is `GraphicsDevice.DrawPrimitives`, which this binding still does not project. Pre-correction SHA-256 of the aggregate f7f51d39472b031067fd44cf995eba4c401562f2f8ab18def620054308bbeebb, of the per-milestone file 518b95c04bbeab2668029494b02b02e8f242f69db7779e43dba826d63321fa96. Corrected a sixth time when GraphicsDevice's draw slice landed: the element before the const_defined? census -- 'does GraphicsDevice define any of the five Draw* members?' -- is now true for the three that read the device's own bound buffers and still false for the two user-primitive families. This row's claim is unchanged and is now carried by the enum itself: PrimitiveType is still a pure-managed enum taking its four values from its own IL, no primitive or topology constant is bound, and the three draw routes take the topology as a plain scalar argument rather than through any constant. The draw members are in fact this enum's first real consumers, which is the opposite of what the census was written to watch for and is recorded here rather than left to look like a regression.
